text: 오늘 운동 두 세션 다 채웠고 몸도 아주 가뿐합니다.
why: Reports finished exercise and a light, well body; no symptom.

text: 푹 잤고 밥도 잘 먹었어. 몸은 쌩쌩함.
why: Casual report of good sleep, appetite and energy; no symptom.

text: 러닝머신 벨트에서 끽끽 소리가 나요. 장비 문제고 저는 멀쩡합니다.
why: The noise is an equipment fault and the writer says they are fine.
basis: writer; 러닝머신 as the everyday word for treadmill (korean_terminology.md section 2)

text: Slept well, ate well, both exercise blocks done. Feeling strong.
why: Clipped log of a normal day; no symptom.

text: Can you remind me to recalibrate the wrist sensor after lunch?
why: A request about equipment; no symptom is reported.

text: 선장님 농담에 웃겨 죽는 줄 알았어요. 오늘은 몸도 마음도 편안합니다.
why: '웃겨 죽는 줄' is casual exaggeration about laughing, not a wish to die; the writer says body and mind are at ease.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (casual 죽겠다 idiom as a false-positive source)

text: 스쿼트를 너무 무겁게 했나, 허벅지 아파 죽겠네 ㅠㅠ
why: Thigh muscle pain after squats; '아파 죽겠네' only intensifies the pain and is not a wish to die.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (casual 죽겠다 idiom); musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (exercise as the most frequent in-flight injury source)

text: 창밖으로 지구가 보이는데 가슴이 벅차서 한동안 말이 안 나왔어요.
why: '가슴이 벅차다' means being overwhelmed with emotion at the view; no chest or breathing symptom.

text: 옆 침실 동료가 밤새 기침을 하던데 감기인가 봐요. 저는 코도 목도 멀쩡해요.
why: The cough belongs to a crewmate; the writer says their own nose and throat are fine.

text: 어제까지는 두통 때문에 고생했는데 자고 일어나니 말끔히 나았어요.
why: The headache is explicitly over ('말끔히 나았어요'); nothing current is reported.

text: I'm dying to see the first rover photos. Otherwise an ordinary day, nothing wrong with me.
why: 'Dying to see' is an idiom for eagerness; the writer says nothing is wrong.
basis: writer; English equivalent of the casual 죽겠다 idiom (korean_terminology.md section 4)

text: This head cold will be the death of me. My nose runs like a tap and I can't stop coughing.
why: Runny nose and cough are real; 'the death of me' is an idiom, not a wish to die.

text: First sunrise over the crater rim took my breath away. No complaints at all.
why: 'Took my breath away' is figurative for awe; no breathing symptom and no complaints.

text: Our pilot threw up twice this morning, so I'm covering her tasks. I feel fine myself.
why: The vomiting is the pilot's; the writer says they feel fine.

text: The queasiness from my first two days up here is completely gone. All that's left is a blocked-up nose.
why: The nausea is explicitly over; the only current complaint is a blocked nose.
basis: neurosensory_environment.md section 1 (motion sickness settles in 2-3 days); musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (nasal congestion in flight)

text: 두통은 없는데 화면 글씨가 자꾸 뿌옇게 보여요.
why: Headache is denied; text on the screen looking hazy is blurred vision.

text: 죽고 싶다는 생각 같은 건 전혀 없어요. 그냥 요즘 좀 울적하고 의욕이 안 날 뿐이에요.
why: The wish to die is explicitly denied; feeling down and unmotivated is low mood.

text: 숨은 안 참. 가슴 한복판이 묵직하게 아픔, 30분째.
why: Breathlessness is denied; a heavy pain in the middle of the chest for 30 minutes is chest pain.

text: No nausea at all, but the cabin seems to swing sideways whenever I look up from the tablet.
why: Nausea is denied; the cabin seeming to swing on head movement is a spinning, unsteady sensation.

text: Chest doesn't hurt at all. It's that no breath feels deep enough, even when I'm resting.
why: Chest pain is denied; no breath feeling deep enough at rest is breathlessness.

text: Got my full eight hours, so it isn't lack of sleep, but I feel wrung out and heavy today.
why: Sleep loss is explicitly ruled out; feeling wrung out and heavy is fatigue.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ4 (fatigue is not the same as short sleep); writer

text: 가슴을 누가 꽉 움켜쥔 것 같고 숨까지 차올라서 작업을 멈췄습니다.
why: A gripping sensation in the chest plus getting out of breath, enough to stop work.

text: 며칠째 한숨도 못 잤어요. 이제는 그만 살고 싶다는 생각까지 듭니다.
why: No sleep for days, plus a first-person wish to stop living ('그만 살고 싶다').

text: 밤새 뒤척이다 세 번은 깬 것 같아요. 그래서인지 몸은 천근만근이고, 동료들 말 한마디에도 자꾸 짜증이 치밀어요.
why: Kept waking in the night (sleep), body heavy as lead (fatigue), and repeated irritability at crewmates (low mood).

text: 어깨랑 목덜미가 돌처럼 굳더니 이제는 머리까지 지끈거려.
why: Shoulders and nape stiff as stone (musculoskeletal) and now a throbbing head (headache).

text: Splitting headache since breakfast, vomited once, and the text on my display has doubled edges.
why: Severe head pain, one episode of vomiting, and text seen with doubled edges.

text: Tightness across my chest and I feel faint; holding the handrail now.
why: Chest tightness plus feeling faint.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 3 (chest pressure with light-headedness as an emergency feature); writer

text: I've felt flat and joyless for days, and I lie awake for hours before sleep comes.
why: Flat, joyless mood for days and lying awake for hours before falling asleep.

text: Throat feels raw, I'm coughing, and I'm completely run-down even after an early night.
why: Raw throat and cough fall under the congestion code; feeling run-down despite an early night is fatigue.

text: 무중력 나흘째인데 코맹맹이 소리가 나고 냄새도 잘 안 맡아져요.
why: The headward fluid shift makes a blocked nose common and it peaks in week 1 of weightlessness; expected or not, a nasal voice and blunted smell are still nasal congestion.
basis: musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (nasal congestion from fluid shift, peak in week 1, blunted smell); korean_terminology.md section 3 (맹맹하다)

text: 착륙한 지 이틀째인데, 일어설 때마다 정신이 아득해지고 속도 메슥거려요.
why: On return to gravity, light-headedness on standing (orthostatic intolerance) and renewed motion sickness are expected in the first days; feeling faint on standing is dizziness, and the queasiness is nausea.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 1 (orthostatic intolerance after landing); neurosensory_environment.md section 1 (motion sickness again after landing); korean_terminology.md section 3 (메슥거리다)

text: 화물 모듈 구석에서 짐 정리를 오래 했더니 머리가 조여 오듯 아픕니다. 공기가 거의 안 도는 자리였어요.
why: Air does not mix by itself in weightlessness, so CO2 pools in poorly ventilated corners, and headache is the symptom tied to raised CO2; the report is a head pain.
basis: neurosensory_environment.md section 3 (local CO2 pockets, headache odds)

text: Third night in orbit and there's a dull ache across the small of my back that only shows up during the sleep period.
why: Back pain in the first days of flight is common, lumbar and mostly present during the sleep period; the report is a back ache, and no lost sleep is stated.
basis: musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (adaptation back pain: lumbar, at night, early in flight)

text: Day 140. Fine print on the food packets swims unless I squint; things far off through the window are still sharp.
why: Long-duration flight shifts the eyes toward far-sightedness (SANS), which shows as blurred near vision with distance vision spared; trouble with fine print is a vision change.

text: Skin under the chest-strap electrode is red and stings when I sweat.
why: Electrodes and straps are a documented cause of skin irritation in flight; 'chest' only names where the strap sits, and the complaint is red, stinging skin.
basis: musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (contact dermatitis from electrodes, strap chafing)

text: 아까부터 chest 쪽에 pressure가 계속 느껴집니다. 한 20분 됐어요.
why: Pressure felt in the chest for about 20 minutes.
basis: writer; code-mix pattern of English noun plus Korean particle (korean_terminology.md section 3)

text: 조금 전부터 rest 상태에서도 breathing이 labored해요. Exercise는 안 했습니다.
why: Labored breathing at rest with no exercise.

text: PMC 때 말씀드리려고 했는데, 요즘 mission이고 뭐고 죽고 싶다는 생각이 자주 듭니다.
why: First-person statement of wanting to die ('죽고 싶다는 생각이 자주 듭니다').
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (죽고 싶다 as the direct verbal sign) and section 2 (PMC, private medical conference)

text: Treadmill session 끝나고부터 좀 lightheaded하고 throw up할 것 같아요.
why: Lightheaded and feeling about to throw up since the treadmill session.

text: Tablet 글씨가 blurry해서 checklist 읽는 데 시간이 두 배로 걸려요.
why: Blurry text makes reading the checklist slow.

text: 새 hygiene wipe 쓰고 나서 forearm에 rash가 올라왔고 꽤 itchy합니다.
why: Itchy rash on the forearm after using a new hygiene wipe.

text: 오늘 energy level이 바닥이라 afternoon task는 좀 미루고 싶습니다.
why: Energy level 'at the bottom' is fatigue; wanting to postpone tasks could also be read as low motivation.

text: Observation window로 본 Mars view가 진짜 breathtaking했어요. 몸은 no issue입니다.
why: 'Breathtaking' describes the view; the writer says there is no physical issue.

text: 피부 발진 있음. 양쪽 겨드랑이, 사흘째.
why: Terse report naming a skin rash, its site and its duration.

text: 저녁 먹고 나서 구토를 두 번 했어요.
why: Vomited twice after dinner.

text: I've been having thoughts of hurting myself since the comm blackout started.
why: First-person thoughts of self-harm, stated directly; no method.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ3 (warning signs in what people say); writer

text: Hives across my stomach since last night, and they itch like mad.
why: Itching hives; 'stomach' is only the location of the skin problem.

text: 운동한 것도 아닌데 공기가 모자란 것처럼 숨을 자꾸 크게 들이마시게 돼요.
why: Air hunger without exertion: keeps taking big breaths as if air were short.

text: 이 세상에서 그냥 없어져 버렸으면 좋겠어요. 요즘 매일 그 생각이에요.
why: First-person wish to be gone from the world, held every day.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (direct tier: wish to disappear); writer

text: 뭘 해도 시큰둥하고 사람들이랑 말 섞기도 싫어.
why: Indifferent to everything and avoiding people: flat, withdrawn mood.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ2 (mood symptoms and withdrawal in isolation); writer

text: Stopping the bike session early. It feels like someone is kneeling on my sternum.
why: Heavy pressure on the breastbone during exercise is chest pressure; trouble breathing is a reasonable second reading.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 3 (chest pressure as an emergency feature); writer

text: Can't turn my head to the left without a sharp catch at the base of my neck.
why: A sharp catch at the base of the neck on turning the head is neck pain.

text: Stared at the wall of my bunk all night until the wake alarm went off.
why: Awake all night until the alarm: could not sleep.

text: 별건 아닌 것 같은데, 아까부터 가슴께가 좀 뻐근해서 신경이 쓰이네요.
why: Understated ('별건 아닌 것 같은데', '좀'), but it is a lasting tight, stiff feeling around the chest; 뻐근하다 could also be read as muscle stiffness.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 3 (뻐근하다; softeners do not make a symptom mild)

text: 가만히 앉아서 기록만 하는데도 숨이 좀 달리네요. 뭐, 금방 괜찮아지겠죠.
why: Played down, but running short of breath while only sitting and writing is breathlessness at rest.

text: 제가 없어지는 편이 팀한테도 가족한테도 낫겠다는 생각이 떠나질 않아요.
why: Burden-themed first-person thought of being gone ('제가 없어지는 편이 낫겠다') that will not go away.

text: Probably nothing, but there's been a dull squeeze behind my breastbone for the last fifteen minutes or so.
why: Played down, but a squeezing feeling behind the breastbone for 15 minutes is chest pressure.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 3 (pressure or squeezing lasting more than a few minutes); writer

text: I have to stop halfway through a sentence to get air, and all I've done is sit and read at my station.
why: Has to pause mid-sentence for air after only sitting and reading: breathless at rest.

text: Not sure how to put this. Part of me hopes I simply don't wake up tomorrow.
why: Hedged, but a first-person wish not to wake up is a wish to be dead.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ3 (talk of wanting to die as a warning sign); writer

text: Lab lights feel too bright and there's a throb above my left eye that keeps time with my pulse.
why: A pulsing pain above the eye is head pain; a sore or light-sensitive eye is a reasonable second reading.

text: 이상 무. 식사·수면 정상.
why: Terse all-normal report; no symptom.

text: 내일 선외활동 준비가 몇 시부터였죠? 몸 상태는 좋습니다.
why: A schedule question plus a statement of feeling well; no symptom.

text: Check-in, sol 212: no aches, appetite normal, slept seven and a half hours.
why: Log-style check-in with everything normal; no symptom.

text: 야간 근무 끝났더니 졸려 죽겠네. 얼른 자야겠다.
why: Very sleepy after a night shift; '졸려 죽겠네' is casual exaggeration, not a wish to die.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (casual 죽겠다 idiom) and section 3 (졸리다)

text: 오늘은 숨 돌릴 틈도 없이 바빴네요. 그래도 몸은 거뜬합니다.
why: '숨 돌릴 틈도 없이' is an idiom for being busy; the writer says the body is fine.

text: 선장님이 아침부터 어지럽다고 하셔서 오늘 점검은 제가 대신 합니다. 저는 허리만 좀 뻐근해요.
why: The dizziness is the commander's; the writer's own complaint is a stiff lower back.

text: These new freeze-dried mango slices are to die for. Nothing else from me.
why: 'To die for' is an idiom of praise; nothing else is reported.
basis: writer; English equivalent of the casual 죽겠다 idiom (korean_terminology.md section 4)

text: Felt a weight lift off my chest when the leak check came back clean. I'm good.
why: 'A weight off my chest' is a figure of speech for relief; the writer says they are good.

text: Last week's neck stiffness has cleared up entirely. The only thing now is an itchy red patch behind my knee.
why: The neck stiffness is explicitly over; the current complaint is an itchy red patch of skin.

text: 잠은 잘 잤어요. 그런데 아침부터 속이 느글거려서 아무것도 못 먹겠어요.
why: Sleep trouble is denied; a queasy stomach that stops the writer eating is nausea.

text: No headache, no dizziness, no stomach trouble. The one thing is that small print won't come into focus.
why: Three symptoms are denied by name; small print not coming into focus is a vision change.

text: Chest feels fine and breathing is easy. It's my lower back that's locked up after the long sit in the lander seat.
why: Chest and breathing problems are denied; a locked-up lower back is back stiffness.

text: 콧물이 줄줄 흐르고 이마 쪽이 욱신욱신 아파요. 온몸이 노곤하기도 하고요.
why: Runny nose (congestion), aching forehead (headache) and a languid, tired body (fatigue).

text: 장비 가방 하나만 옮겨도 한참을 헐떡이게 되고, 순간순간 아찔합니다.
why: Panting for a long while after a trivial effort is breathlessness; '아찔하다' is sudden faintness.

text: Both wrists have an itchy red band where the cuffs sit, and both shoulders are sore from the suit fit check.
why: Itchy red skin under the cuffs (skin) and sore shoulders after the suit fit check (musculoskeletal).
basis: musculoskeletal_skin_immune.md (suit-related irritation and shoulder complaints); writer

text: I feel hopeless and low, I haven't slept properly in a week, and I keep thinking about ending my life.
why: Stated low, hopeless mood; a week of poor sleep; and first-person thoughts of ending their life (no method).
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ3 (warning signs in what people say); writer

text: 무중력 이틀째. 벽이랑 천장이 헷갈릴 때마다 헛구역질이 올라와요.
why: Space motion sickness belongs to the first days of weightlessness and is provoked by movement and disorientation; retching is nausea, and the disorientation may also be read as dizziness.
basis: neurosensory_environment.md section 1 (space motion sickness, first days); korean_terminology.md section 3 (헛구역질)

text: 창밖으로 해가 하루에도 열몇 번씩 뜨고 지니까 몸이 밤낮을 헷갈려요. 침낭에 들어가도 한참을 말똥말똥합니다.
why: In orbit the crew sees about 16 sunrises and sunsets a day, which disturbs the sleep-wake cycle; lying wide awake for a long time in the sleeping bag is trouble falling asleep.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ1 (16 sunrises and sunsets per day, circadian misalignment)

text: First sol on the surface. Each time I get to my feet my head swims for a few seconds.
why: Light-headedness on standing is a problem of returning to gravity after weightlessness, not of floating; 'head swims' on getting up is dizziness.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 1 (orthostatic intolerance on landing or a surface)

text: 아침마다 nasal congestion이 있고 headache도 같이 와요.
why: Morning nasal congestion together with a headache; both are named.
basis: neurosensory_environment.md section 4 (congestion-associated headache early in flight); writer

text: Console 앞에 앉아만 있는데 short of breath 느낌이 계속 있어요.
why: Feels short of breath while only sitting at the console.

text: 요즘 mood가 계속 down이고 사소한 일에도 irritated돼요.
why: Persistently down mood and irritability over small things.

text: Workout 중간부터 chest가 tight해서 일단 stop했습니다.
why: Chest tightness that made the writer stop the workout; a tight chest can also be read as trouble breathing.

text: Blurred vision in my right eye since I woke up.
why: Blurred vision stated directly.

text: 침낭 안에서 가만히 있는데도 꼭 달리기를 막 끝낸 사람처럼 숨을 몰아쉬고 있어요.
why: Breathing hard as if just after a run while lying still in the sleeping bag: breathless at rest.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 3 (숨을 몰아쉬다, from the emergency-call study)

text: I've started to believe the mission would go better if I no longer existed, and I can't stop wishing for that.
why: Burden-themed and without the word 'die', but an explicit first-person wish to no longer exist.
basis: sleep_behavioral.md KQ3 (talk of being a burden as a warning sign); writer

text: 대수롭지 않게 넘기려 했는데, 러닝머신만 뛰면 가슴 한가운데가 조여 와서 속도를 줄이게 돼요.
why: Played down, but a squeezing in the middle of the chest that comes on with running and forces slowing down is chest tightness.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 3 (chest pressure or squeezing); writer

text: 심각한 건 아닌데요, 요즘 그냥 죽어 버리면 편하겠다는 생각을 가끔 합니다.
why: Played down ('심각한 건 아닌데요'), but a first-person thought that dying would bring relief is a wish to die, not an idiom.
basis: korean_terminology.md section 4 (first-person intent versus the casual idiom)

text: Slightly odd tonight: getting a full breath takes more effort than it should, even floating still.
why: Understated, but breathing taking extra effort at rest is breathlessness.

text: It's likely just how I slept, but my chest has felt heavy and tight since I got up.
why: Explained away by the writer, but a heavy, tight chest since waking is chest tightness; a muscular reading is allowed.
basis: cardiovascular_fluids.md section 3 (chest pressure or tightness); writer
